config.title: File uploads

intro.title: File uploads
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a simple Express server that accepts file uploads from a user. You'll learn how to handle multipart/form-data using the multer middleware to process uploaded files. The core concepts include configuring middleware, managing file storage, and accessing uploaded file details in your routes. By the end, you'll have a working endpoint that can receive and save files to your server's filesystem.
intro.usecase: File uploads are essential in countless real-world applications where users need to submit documents, images, or media. You'll implement this pattern in user profile forms for avatar pictures, in content management dashboards for uploading articles with images, and in e-commerce platforms for product photo galleries. As a developer, you'll handle uploads in customer support systems for attaching screenshots, in document-sharing applications like Google Drive alternatives, and in social media platforms where users post photos and videos. Understanding Express file uploads prepares you to build these common features that require secure, efficient handling of user-generated files.

objectives: Configure an Express application to handle multipart/form-data requests
Implement middleware for processing file uploads in an Express route
Construct a file upload endpoint that accepts and stores uploaded files
Apply validation to restrict file types and sizes during upload
Initialize a static file-serving mechanism to make uploaded files accessible
Integrate file upload functionality into a complete Express application workflow
Manipulate uploaded file metadata to generate unique filenames and paths

steps.title: Import Express, multer, and path modules
steps.instruction: Import the Express framework, multer middleware for handling file uploads, and the path module for file path operations. Write the import statements at the top of your file.
steps.hint: Use the require() function to import each module. Express is the main framework, multer handles file uploads, and path helps with file paths.
steps.seedCode: // Import Express, multer, and path modules here
steps.expectedOutcome: Your file will have the three required modules imported and ready to use for building the file upload functionality.
successCriteria: Express, multer, and path modules are imported using require() statements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some modules, but not all three. Make sure to import Express, multer, and path modules using require() statements.
steps.feedbackWrong: The required modules aren't imported correctly. You need to import Express, multer, and path modules using require() statements at the top of your file.

steps.title: Initialize Express application
steps.instruction: Create an Express app instance by calling the imported express() function and assign it to a constant named 'app'.
steps.hint: Use the imported 'express' module to create your application instance. The express module is a function that returns an Express application when called.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have an Express application instance ready to configure for handling file uploads.
successCriteria: An Express app instance is created and assigned to a constant named 'app'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're calling the imported express() function to create the app instance and assigning it to a constant named 'app'.
steps.feedbackWrong: create an Express app instance by calling the imported express() function and store it in a constant named 'app'.

steps.title: Configure multer storage and file filter
steps.instruction: Configure multer's disk storage by creating a storage object that specifies a destination folder and a filename function, and create a file filter function that only accepts image files.
steps.hint: Use multer.diskStorage() with destination and filename properties. For the file filter, check the file's mimetype to see if it starts with 'image/'.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a storage configuration object and a file filter function ready for use with multer.
successCriteria: A multer diskStorage object is created with destination and filename functions, and a fileFilter function is defined that accepts only image files.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've included both the storage configuration and the file filter function. Make sure the file filter checks for image mimetypes.
steps.feedbackWrong: The configuration isn't quite right. Remember to use multer.diskStorage() for storage and create a separate fileFilter function. Check the syntax for both.

steps.title: Create multer upload middleware instance
steps.instruction: Create a multer instance named 'upload' using the storage and fileFilter configuration you previously defined.
steps.hint: Call multer() with an object containing your storage and fileFilter configurations.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a configured multer middleware instance ready to handle file uploads.
successCriteria: A constant named 'upload' is created by calling multer() with storage and fileFilter properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling multer() with an object containing both storage and fileFilter properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The multer instance wasn't created correctly. Review how to initialize multer with configuration options.

steps.title: Create uploads directory if it doesn't exist
steps.instruction: Use the fs module to check if the 'uploads' directory exists and create it synchronously if it doesn't.
steps.hint: You'll need to import the fs module and use fs.existsSync() and fs.mkdirSync() methods.
steps.expectedOutcome: The 'uploads' directory will be created automatically when the server starts if it doesn't already exist.
successCriteria: The fs module is imported and used to check existence and create the uploads directory synchronously.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using fs.existsSync() to check and fs.mkdirSync() to create the directory.
steps.feedbackWrong: The directory creation logic is missing or incorrect. Remember to import fs and use existsSync/mkdirSync methods.

steps.title: Create POST endpoint for file upload
steps.instruction: Define a POST route at '/upload' that uses the multer upload middleware to handle single file uploads.
steps.hint: Use app.post() with the route path and middleware, then add a route handler function that sends a response.
steps.expectedOutcome: A POST route '/upload' is created that uses the multer middleware to accept single file uploads.
successCriteria: The code includes app.post('/upload', upload.single('file'), handler) with a route handler function that sends a response.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to include the route path '/upload', the upload.single('file') middleware, and a route handler function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The POST endpoint is not correctly defined. Review how to set up a route with middleware in Express.

steps.title: Add file validation in upload handler
steps.instruction: Inside your POST route handler, add validation to check if a file was uploaded and log the file details.
steps.hint: Access the uploaded file from req.file. Check if it exists, then log its filename and mimetype.
steps.expectedOutcome: The route handler now validates that a file was uploaded and logs its details.
successCriteria: The POST route handler includes a check for req.file and logs the filename and mimetype.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're checking req.file and logging both filename and mimetype.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validation is missing or incomplete. Check if req.file exists and log its properties.

steps.title: Add error handling for upload failures
steps.instruction: Inside your POST route handler, add a try-catch block to handle potential errors during file upload processing.
steps.hint: Wrap the existing upload logic in a try block, then add a catch block to send an appropriate error response.
steps.expectedOutcome: The POST route handler will have basic error handling structure with try-catch blocks.
successCriteria: The route handler contains a try block and a catch block that handles errors.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both try and catch blocks in your route handler.
steps.feedbackWrong: The route handler doesn't have proper error handling structure. Add try-catch blocks to handle potential upload errors.

steps.title: Create static file serving for uploaded files
steps.instruction: Add Express static middleware to serve files from the 'uploads' directory.
steps.hint: Use app.use() with express.static() and specify the directory path.
steps.analogousExample:
// Serving static files from a 'public' directory
app.use(express.static('public'));
steps.expectedOutcome: Uploaded files in the 'uploads' directory will be accessible via HTTP requests.
successCriteria: express.static middleware is configured to serve files from the 'uploads' directory.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using app.use() with express.static() and specifying 'uploads' as the directory path.
steps.feedbackWrong: The static file serving isn't configured correctly. Review how to use express.static middleware.

steps.title: Start the Express server
steps.instruction: Start the Express server by calling app.listen() on port 3000 and log a message when the server starts.
steps.hint: Use app.listen() with the port number and a callback function that logs a message to the console.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will be ready to accept file upload requests on port 3000.
successCriteria: The app.listen() method is called with port 3000 and a callback that logs a server start message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've called app.listen() with the correct port and a callback function that logs a message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server isn't started yet. Use app.listen() to start the server on port 3000 with a callback that logs a message.
